title: Weil divisor data of an invertible sheaf on an open normal affine scheme
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian normal domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and put $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. Write $H(A)$ for the nonzero prime ideals with no prime strictly between them and $(0)$ [def-trf-affine-weil-divisor-class-group]. For $\mathfrak r\in H(A)$, let $v_{\mathfrak r}:K^\times\to\mathbf Z$ be the normalized valuation of the discrete valuation ring $A_{\mathfrak r}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Let $U$ be a nonempty open subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion], and let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_U$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. There exists a finitely supported family of integers $(d_{\mathfrak r})_{\mathfrak r\in H(A)\cap U}$ with both of the following properties. For every point $\mathfrak t\in U$, there exists $a_{\mathfrak t}\in K^\times$ such that $d_{\mathfrak r}=v_{\mathfrak r}(a_{\mathfrak t})$ for every $\mathfrak r\in H(A)$ contained in $\mathfrak t$. Moreover, $L\cong\mathcal O_U$ if and only if there exists $a\in K^\times$ such that $d_{\mathfrak r}=v_{\mathfrak r}(a)$ for every $\mathfrak r\in H(A)\cap U$.

source.place: Tags 02SG (lemma-divisor-meromorphic-locally-finite), 0BE6 (definition-divisor-invertible-sheaf), and 0BE8 (lemma-normal-c1-injective), including the proof by dividing a rational section by a rational function; the local equations are the coefficients in a local frame used in definition-order-vanishing-meromorphic. Here U is Noetherian, so locally finite support is finite.

proof.text: Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\eta=(0)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field], $X$ is integral, $k(X)=K$, and its stalk at $\mathfrak t$ is $A_{\mathfrak t}$. The open subscheme structure of [def-weil-open-immersion] identifies $\mathcal O_{U,\mathfrak t}$ with the same stalk. The nonempty open $U$ is integral: its space is irreducible because any two nonempty opens in it are nonempty opens in $X$, and its restricted structure sheaf is reduced because that of $X$ is reduced. Thus it satisfies the reduced-and-irreducible characterization of [def-pc-integral-scheme], with the same generic point and function field. By [lem-sc-invertible-module-generic-stalk], $L_\eta$ is a one-dimensional $K$-vector space, the maps $L_{\mathfrak t}\to L_\eta$ are injective, and an element of $L_\eta$ is a regular section on $U$ exactly when it belongs to every stalk image.

source.place: Tag 01X5 (lemma-meromorphic-functions-integral-scheme), and the integral case of Tag 02OZ (lemma-regular-meromorphic-section-exists)

proof.text: Choose a nonempty trivializing open $W\subseteq U$ and a frame $e\in L(W)$ using [def-sc-invertible-module]. By the basic-open basis of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open], choose $0\ne f\in A$ with $D(f)\subseteq W$. Take $s=e_\eta\in L_\eta\setminus\{0\}$. On $D(f)$ this chosen rational section is already a regular frame. For every $\mathfrak r\in H(A)\cap U$, choose a generator $e_{\mathfrak r}$ of $L_{\mathfrak r}$ and write $s=b_{\mathfrak r}(e_{\mathfrak r})_\eta$ with $b_{\mathfrak r}\in K^\times$, using [lem-sc-invertible-module-generic-stalk].

source.place: Tag 02OZ, integral case; Tag 02SG (lemma-divisor-meromorphic-locally-finite), first sentence of proof

proof.text: Set $d_{\mathfrak r}=v_{\mathfrak r}(b_{\mathfrak r})$. This is independent of the generator: if $e'_{\mathfrak r}=u e_{\mathfrak r}$ with $u\in A_{\mathfrak r}^\times$, then $b'_{\mathfrak r}=b_{\mathfrak r}/u$. The valuation homomorphism and unit criterion of [lem-trf-normal-domain-principal-divisor-kernel] give $v_{\mathfrak r}(u)=0$, hence equal values. The cited node applies to $A$, which is a Noetherian normal domain, and supplies exactly the normalized valuations in the statement. For $\mathfrak r\in D(f)$, use the frame of Step 2; its coefficient is $1$, so $d_{\mathfrak r}=0$.

A prime in the support therefore contains $f$. Such a prime $\mathfrak r$ is minimal among primes containing $(f)$: a smaller prime containing $f\ne0$ would be a nonzero prime strictly between $(0)$ and the height-one prime $\mathfrak r$. By [lem-sc-finite-minimal-primes-over-ideal], there are only finitely many minimal primes over $(f)$ in the Noetherian ring $A$. Hence the family $(d_{\mathfrak r})$ has finite support. This also handles $D(f)=X$, when the support is empty.

source.place: Tag 02SG, proof via components of the complement of a nonempty trivializing open; affine version using algebra.tex Tag 00FR

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak t\in U$. Choose a frame $e$ of $L$ on an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq U$ of $\mathfrak t$, using [def-sc-invertible-module], and write $s=a_{\mathfrak t}e_\eta$, $a_{\mathfrak t}\in K^\times$, using [lem-sc-invertible-module-generic-stalk]. Every $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak t$ lies in $V$: indeed $\mathfrak t$ is in the closure of $\{\mathfrak r\}$ in the spectrum, so any open containing $\mathfrak t$ contains $\mathfrak r$. At such a height-one prime the germ of $e$ is a generator and its coefficient for $s$ is precisely $a_{\mathfrak t}$. The generator independence in Step 3 gives $d_{\mathfrak r}=v_{\mathfrak r}(a_{\mathfrak t})$. This proves the local-equation clause, including that all of its indexed primes lie in $U$.

source.place: Tag 02SF, coefficient of a meromorphic section in a local frame

proof.text: Suppose $d_{\mathfrak r}=v_{\mathfrak r}(a)$ on $H(A)\cap U$ for some $a\in K^\times$. Put $t=a^{-1}s\in L_\eta$. Fix $\mathfrak t\in U$ and the local frame of Step 5; the coefficient of $t$ is $c=a_{\mathfrak t}/a$. Set $R=A_{\mathfrak t}$. This is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] and a normal domain with fraction field $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain]. By [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization](1), its height-one primes correspond to $\mathfrak r\in H(A)$ contained in $\mathfrak t$: contraction preserves strict chains and zero. All these $\mathfrak r$ lie in $U$ by Step 5. By [lem-weil-pbc-localize-localization-at-prime](1), their local rings are $A_{\mathfrak r}$, with the same embeddings in $K$, so their normalized valuations are $v_{\mathfrak r}$. Step 5 and the assumed equality give $v_{\mathfrak r}(c)=0$. The unit-kernel criterion of [lem-trf-normal-domain-principal-divisor-kernel], now applied to $R$, yields $c\in R^\times$. Thus $t$ belongs to $L_{\mathfrak t}$ and generates it, for every $\mathfrak t\in U$.

source.place: Tag 0BE8 (lemma-normal-c1-injective), proof: divide the rational section by the rational function and apply the normal-domain unit criterion locally

proof.text: By [lem-sc-invertible-module-generic-stalk](3), $t$ from Step 6 is the generic germ of a global regular section $\tau\in L(U)$. Injectivity on stalks in part (2) shows that its germ at each $\mathfrak t$ is the generating germ already found there. The map $\mathcal O_U\to L$, $1\mapsto\tau$, is an isomorphism: on a trivializing open write $\tau=h e$; at each point $h$ has a unit germ, hence has a local inverse (represent the inverse germ on a smaller neighbourhood and shrink until the product is $1$). These local inverses define inverses to the module map and agree on overlaps. Therefore $L\cong\mathcal O_U$. Conversely, if $L$ is trivial, let $e\in L(U)$ be a global frame and write $s=a e_\eta$ for the unique $a\in K^\times$, using part (1) of the same node. At every height-one prime the coefficient in this frame is $a$, and Step 3 gives $d_{\mathfrak r}=v_{\mathfrak r}(a)$. This proves the other implication for the same family chosen in Step 3.

lean.statement: theorem normal_open_line_weil_dictionary {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsIntegrallyClosed A] (U : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Opens) (hU : Nonempty U) (L : U.toScheme.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] : ∃ d : {q : Ring.WeilHeightOnePrime A // q.val ∈ U} →₀ ℤ, (∀ t : PrimeSpectrum A, t ∈ U → ∃ a : (FractionRing A)ˣ, ∀ q : {q : Ring.WeilHeightOnePrime A // q.val ∈ U}, q.val.val.asIdeal ≤ t.asIdeal → d q = Ring.weilFractionOrder q.val a.val) ∧ (Nonempty (L ≅ SheafOfModules.unit U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) ↔ ∃ a : (FractionRing A)ˣ, ∀ q : {q : Ring.WeilHeightOnePrime A // q.val ∈ U}, d q = Ring.weilFractionOrder q.val a.val)
